reading.body:
At 1.6 MW of published IT capacity, this campus is small by any AI-infrastructure measure. Assuming 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 1.6 MW supports roughly 40 racks, and the arithmetic does not change meaningfully at 10 or 20 kW per rack. The 43,294 square feet of technical space is generous relative to that power figure, which suggests the floor was sized for density headroom or traditional enterprise loads rather than high-density GPU clusters. Neither total power nor any expansion capacity beyond 1.6 MW is published.

The certification stack is broad and compliance-oriented. SOC 1 Type 2 and SOC 2 Type 2 qualify the campus for regulated enterprise workloads requiring audited controls. PCI DSS qualifies it for payment-card data environments. ITAR qualifies it for export-controlled defense and aerospace data. NIST 800-53 and HITRUST together qualify it for federal-adjacent and healthcare workloads. SSAE 18 is the auditing standard underlying the SOC reports rather than a separate capability. Taken together, the certifications describe a campus built for compliance-sensitive tenants, not raw compute scale.

Within Colorado, this site holds the second rank among the two facilities on this site that publish a megawatt figure, out of 17 mapped facilities total. Those two facilities together show 19.6 MW of published IT capacity, and this campus accounts for 1.6 MW of that, roughly eight percent. Fifteen of the seventeen mapped Colorado facilities publish no capacity figure at all, so the state picture is incomplete. At its published scale, this campus is a compliance-ready colocation facility rather than a node that moves the needle on AI capacity in Colorado.
